Developer Pages

Create your own pages in a MOLGENIS database using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript

Overview

The Page Editor is an EMX2 feature where you can create and edit custom pages in MOLGENIS using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. This option may be useful if you want to go beyond the features that are offered in the Page Builder.

Get started

Here's how to create your own developer page

  1. Sign in and go to the Page Gallery
  2. Click the "Add New Page" button
  3. Select the "Developer page" option and click the "create page" button. Enter a name for the page and save
  4. In the Page Gallery, click the edit button for your page in the gallery
  5. Start building your page!

Tips

Here are a few tips to further enhance your page, which are settings that can be accessed via Developer pages table.

  • You can hook into our tailwind theme To make it easier to build custom pages, you can piggyback off our theme (we use tailwind in our UI). This makes the process of designing pages bit easier and it also allows you to create pages that look and feel like a MOLGENIS page. This setting is enabled by default, but can be disabled by changing the "enable base styles" option to "false".
  • Style buttons like a MOLGENIS button If your page uses buttons, you can use our button styles. Add the attribute type="submit" to your button and our styles will be automatically applied. You can also disable this feature, by changing "enable button styles" to "false". Only primary action buttons are supported.
  • Allow pages to fill the page By default, developer pages have a fixed width. This means that pages do not fill the entire width of the page. This is useful if you are creating landing pages or displaying general information. If you would to maximise the space available, this setting can disabled by changing the setting "enable full screen" to "false".
  • Add external dependencies It is also possible to use external CSS or JavaScript dependencies in your page. To do this, register them in the Dependencies CSS or the Dependencies JS table, and then link them in the page settings menu. WARNING: Adding external dependencies may have unintended side effects with the appearance or functionality of the MOLGENIS UI. If issues arise, remove the dependency from your page.
